messages.subject: gl.fst.pop as table
parts:
Hi all,

Does anyone know the easiest way to convert the output gl.fst.pop into a data table? The output is often scrambled and not in order of populations (in my case 1-17), and I just wanted to sort it to be a table listing populations in order so it can be easily copy pasted in excel etc.

Thanks,
Ella

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: gl.fst.pop as table
parts:
Hi Ella,

Please see code below, I hope this is what you are looking for, otherwise, let me know. 

Cheers,
Luis 

library(dartR)
library(data.table)
res <- gl.fst.pop(platypus.gl)
# converting to data.table
res2 <- as.data.table(res, keep.rownames = TRUE)
# converting matrix to long format
res3 <- melt(res2)
# removing NAs
res4 <- res3[complete.cases(res3$value),]
# renaming column names
colnames(res4) <- c("pop1","pop2","Fst")
# saving as csv file
write.csv(res4,file = "test.csv",row.names = FALSE)
